lead: The working stress method (WSM), also called the elastic method or the modular ratio method, checks a reinforced concrete section under the loads it actually carries in use, with no load factors. Concrete and steel are treated as elastic materials, and the stresses computed from that model must stay below permissible stresses: fixed fractions of the material strengths. IS 456:2000 keeps it in Annex B, and it is still used for water tanks, quick checks and old structures. This chapter gives its assumptions, permissible stresses and design constants, and designs a singly reinforced beam.
prereq: You need: Ec, Es and the strength grades from properties of concrete and reinforcing steel.

items: Plane sections remain plane, so strain varies linearly with distance from the neutral axis.
Concrete in compression and steel are both linear elastic: stress is proportional to strain.
Concrete carries no tension; once it cracks, the steel takes all the tension.
Steel and the concrete around it have the same strain (perfect bond), so a steel area A<sub>st</sub> acts like a concrete area m A<sub>st</sub>.

blocks.text: The modular ratio m converts steel to equivalent concrete. IS 456 fixes m = 280/(3σcbc), where σcbc is the permissible compressive stress in bending, instead of the short-term Es/Ec; this partly allows for creep. For M20, m = 280/(3 × 7) = 13.33, whereas the short-term ratio would be 200,000/22,361 = 8.9.
The permissible stresses of IS 456 Annex B (Tables 21 and 22) are in N/mm²:
For M20, σ<sub>cbc</sub> = 7 N/mm² is about a third of f<sub>ck</sub>; for Fe415, σ<sub>st</sub> = 230 N/mm² is about 0.55f<sub>y</sub>. That margin is the factor of safety of the method.

sections.h3: Neutral axis, balanced section and the constants k, j, Q

blocks.text: For a section of width b and effective depth d (top fibre to the centroid of the tension steel), equating the first moments of the compression concrete and the transformed steel about the neutral axis gives the actual neutral axis depth x:

blocks.where: b and d in mm, A<sub>st</sub> in mm², x in mm. Solve the quadratic for x.

blocks.text: The critical (balanced) neutral axis depth xc = k d is where concrete reaches σcbc and steel reaches σst at the same moment. From the linear strain diagram, the steel stress divided by m and the concrete stress are in the ratio (d − x) : x, which gives
k = mσcbc / (mσcbc + σ<sub>st</sub>),   j = 1 − k/3,   Q = ½ σ<sub>cbc</sub> k j
blocks.where: k is the neutral axis depth factor, j d = z is the lever arm (compression acts at x/3 from the top), and Q in N/mm² is the moment factor, so that the balanced moment of resistance is M<sub>R</sub> = Q b d².

blocks.text: Because mσcbc = 280/3 = 93.33 for every grade, k depends only on the steel: 0.289 for Fe415 and 0.400 for Fe250. With M20 and Fe415, j = 0.904 and Q = 0.5 × 7 × 0.289 × 0.904 = 0.913 N/mm²; with M25 and Fe415, Q = 1.109 N/mm².
Compare the actual x with x<sub>c</sub>:

items: x < xc: under-reinforced. Steel reaches σst first, so MR = σst Ast (d − x/3).
x = x<sub>c</sub>: balanced. Both limits are reached together, M<sub>R</sub> = Q b d².
x > xc: over-reinforced. Concrete reaches σcbc first, so MR = ½ σcbc b x (d − x/3).

sections.h3: Design of a singly reinforced beam by WSM

blocks.text: A singly reinforced beam has tension steel only; the design aims close to balanced, which uses both materials fully.

items: Find the service load, including self-weight (25 kN/m³ for reinforced concrete), and the service moment M.
Pick the width b (often the wall thickness, 230 mm, or 250 mm) and compute m, k, j and Q.
Find the required effective depth d = √(M/(Q b)). Choose the overall depth D = d + effective cover, rounded up.
Find the steel area A<sub>st</sub> = M/(σ<sub>st</sub> j d) and choose bars; check the minimum tension steel 0.85 b d/fy.

Check the actual stresses with the bars provided: solve for x, then σ<sub>cbc</sub> = M/(½ b x (d − x/3)) and σ<sub>st</sub> = M/(A<sub>st</sub> (d − x/3)); both must not exceed the permissible values.
Check shear, bond and deflection separately.

blocks.text: The method predicts service stresses well, but it cannot say how far the member is from collapse; that gap led to the ultimate load method.

examples.question: Design a simply supported rectangular beam of effective span 5 m by the working stress method. Besides its self-weight it carries a uniformly distributed service load of 12 kN/m (finishes and live load). Use M20 concrete and Fe415 steel, a width of 250 mm and an effective cover of 40 mm. Check the stresses with the bars provided.
steps: Permissible stresses: σ<sub>cbc</sub> = 7 N/mm², σ<sub>st</sub> = 230 N/mm²; m = 280/(3 × 7) = 13.33.
A<sub>st</sub> = M/(σ<sub>st</sub> j d) = 47.27 × 10⁶ / (230 × 0.9038 × 460) = 494 mm² (minimum 0.85bd/fy = 236 mm²). Provide 2 bars of 16 mm and 1 of 12 mm: 515 mm².
Actual neutral axis: 250x²/2 = 13.33 × 515 × (460 − x) gives x = 133.9 mm (x<sub>c</sub> = 0.2887 × 460 = 132.8 mm, so the section is just over-reinforced).
examples.answer: A 250 mm × 500 mm beam (d = 460 mm) with 2 bars of 16 mm and 1 bar of 12 mm (515 mm²); under 47.3 kNm the stresses are 6.80 N/mm² in concrete and 221 N/mm² in steel, both within the permissible values.

examples.question: A beam 230 mm wide with an effective depth of 450 mm has 2 bars of 16 mm as tension steel. M20 concrete, Fe415 steel. Find its moment of resistance by WSM and the concrete stress when that moment acts.
steps: Critical depth x<sub>c</sub> = 0.2887 × 450 = 129.9 mm. Since x < x<sub>c</sub> the beam is under-reinforced: steel governs.
Lever arm z = 450 − 123.4/3 = 408.9 mm. M<sub>R</sub> = σ<sub>st</sub> A<sub>st</sub> z = 230 × 402 × 408.9 = 37.8 × 10⁶ Nmm = 37.8 kNm.
Concrete stress at that moment, from the strain diagram: σ<sub>cbc</sub> = (σ<sub>st</sub>/m) × x/(d − x) = (230/13.33) × 123.4/326.6 = 6.52 N/mm² < 7.
examples.answer: Under-reinforced; M<sub>R</sub> = 37.8 kNm, at which concrete is at 6.52 N/mm² and steel at its permissible 230 N/mm².

traps: WSM uses the permissible stresses σ<sub>cbc</sub> and σ<sub>st</sub>, never f<sub>ck</sub> or f<sub>y</sub>: for Fe415 the steel stress is 230 N/mm², not 415 or 361 N/mm².
The IS 456 modular ratio is 280/(3σ<sub>cbc</sub>) = 13.33 for M20, not E<sub>s</sub>/Ec = 8.9; using 8.9 moves the neutral axis up and gives a different k, j and Q.
In an over-reinforced section the moment of resistance comes from the concrete, ½ σ<sub>cbc</sub> b x (d − x/3); writing σ<sub>st</sub> A<sub>st</sub> (d − x/3) for it overstates the capacity.
In WSM the compression acts at x/3 below the top, so z = d − x/3; the 0.42xu of the limit state stress block does not belong here.

quiz.q: State the permissible stresses σ<sub>cbc</sub> for M20 and σ<sub>st</sub> for Fe415 in WSM.
quiz.a: σ<sub>cbc</sub> = 7 N/mm² for M20; σ<sub>st</sub> = 230 N/mm² for Fe415.

quiz.q: Why is k the same, 0.289, for Fe415 bars whatever the concrete grade?
quiz.a: Because mσcbc = 280/3 = 93.33 for every grade, k = 93.33/(93.33 + σ<sub>st</sub>) depends only on σ<sub>st</sub>.

quiz.q: Find the balanced moment of resistance of a 250 mm × 500 mm (effective) beam in M20 with Fe415 bars.
A 300 mm × 550 mm (effective) M20 beam has 4 bars of 16 mm (804 mm²) of Fe415. Is it under- or over-reinforced, and what is its moment of resistance?
quiz.a: 150x² = 13.33 × 804 × (550 − x) gives x = 165.7 mm, above x<sub>c</sub> = 0.2887 × 550 = 158.8 mm, so it is over-reinforced and concrete governs: M<sub>R</sub> = 0.5 × 7 × 300 × 165.7 × (550 − 55.2) = 86.1 kNm.

quiz.q: Why can WSM not tell how safe a beam is against collapse?
quiz.a: It checks only elastic stresses at service load against permissible values. Near failure concrete and steel are not elastic, so the ratio of permissible stress to strength is not the ratio of collapse load to service load.

beyond: Buildings in India are now designed almost entirely by limit state methods, but elastic cracked-section analysis is still how engineers check crack widths and service steel stresses, and liquid-retaining structures to IS 3370 were long designed by working stress. Search next for "cracked transformed section" and "IS 3370 working stress".
